evidence: Cic. Sen. 76: sunt pueritiae studia certa
Ter. Heaut. 183: jam inde ūsque ā pueritiā
terms.comment: Childhood up to about the seventeenth year, though often used more loosely (Lewis & Short); after it comes adulēscentia (see youth). “From childhood” is ā pueritiā, or ā puerō, ā puerīs, “from a boy, from boys”. Horace scans it puertia (C. 1.36.8).

evidence: Quint. 1.1.19: quantum in īnfantiā praesūmptum est temporis
terms.comment: First “inability to speak” (Lucr. 5.1031), and so infancy, early childhood (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: from early childhood, from a little boy

phrases.latin: sunt pueritiae studia certa; num igitur ea dēsīderant adulēscentēs?
phrases.english: childhood has its own pursuits; do young men miss them, then?

phrases.latin: nam mihi magna cum eō jam inde ūsque ā pueritiā fuit semper familiāritās
phrases.english: for he and I have always been close friends, right from childhood

phrases.latin: inde ego hunc majōrem adoptāvī mihi; ēdūxī ā parvulō
phrases.english: so I adopted the elder one as my own; I brought him up from a little boy

sources: Lewis & Short: pueritia · Lewis & Short: infantia · Lewis & Short: parvulus
